summary: Console/runbook login fails after proxy header rewrite causes stale session-cookie validation errors
description:
Issue summary: After an ingress/identity-proxy configuration change rolled out 2026-03-09, a subset of internal users cannot log into the console and internal runbook tool. The login flow completes with Okta SSO but the application rejects the returned session cookie and shows a 401 or immediate redirect to login.

Impact: ~12% of support engineers and oncall cannot access runbooks and the console intermittently; prevents runbook execution for some oncall shifts. Problem is service-affecting for internal tooling during oncall windows.

Environment: Production (us-east), internal runbook portal (runbook.redwood.internal) and console.redwood.internal. Identity-proxy (v2.7.1) and ingress-nginx sidecar recently updated on 2026-03-09.

Observed behavior: Users authenticate via Okta and get redirected back to the console; instead of a persistent session they are bounced to /login with a new redirect. Logs show session validation failures referencing mismatched cookie signature or missing header used in signature calculation.

Expected behavior: Okta SSO completes and persistent session cookie is accepted by runbook and console services.

Notes: This ticket covers investigation, mitigation, and rollout of a fix. Cross-links to identity-proxy PRs and a follow-up runbook will be added.
steps_to_reproduce: 2) Click Sign in -> Okta, complete MFA for a test account (m.chen+support@redwood.com),
3) After redirect back to runbook, observe redirect loop or 401 and check runbook logs for 'session signature mismatch' or 'missing x-session-ts header'.
logs: [runbook-prod-01] 2026-03-10T09:12:34Z ERROR session: validation failed: signature mismatch (expected=abc123, got=)
[ingress-nginx] 2026-03-09T22:03:12Z WARN cookie: SameSite attribute set to Lax by default after config change
comments: Support (Maya Chen) - 2026-03-10: Initial triage found that users complete Okta auth but fail at app session validation. Opening as P1 due to oncall impact.
SRE (Priya Patel) - 2026-03-10: Reproduced with incognito. Observed header reorder at identity-proxy and session-sig header being stripped for some requests. Adding identity-proxy and ingress oncall.

Identity Proxy Eng (Ethan Morales) - 2026-03-11: Recent ingress-nginx update introduced a header rewrite optimization. We shipped a small change to reorder headers for cache locality. Rolling back to confirm.
Support (Maya Chen) - 2026-03-11: Customer-facing note: internal teams informed on #support and ops runbook updated with workaround steps.
SRE (Priya Patel) - 2026-03-12: Rolled back proxy header-rewrite on prod us-east; observed successful logins for previously blocked users. Continuing to monitor; preparing permanent fix.
Reporter (Maya Chen) - 2026-03-12: Verified that two impacted engineers regained access after rollback. Marking verification steps in investigation notes.
investigation:
Timeline: 2026-03-09 ingress/identity-proxy optimization rolled (header reordering + cookie policy tweak). 2026-03-10 multiple login failures reported. Hypothesis: runbook/console session validation depends on canonical header ordering (x-session-ts followed by x-session-sig) when reconstructing signature for legacy session library. The header rewrite changed ordering and some client proxies dropped the x-session-sig header due to SameSite changes.

Findings:
- Identity-proxy change reordered headers; some downstream HTTP/2 multiplexing paths re-serialized headers and dropped empty headers.
- ingress-nginx defaulted SameSite to Lax for cookies which caused the browser to not send the session cookie on some cross-site redirect flows in our internal SSO flow.
- Runbook service session library treats missing x-session-sig as a mismatch rather than a graceful fallback.

Reproducibility: Reproducible in prod with incognito and with a synthetic test that mimics the Okta redirect chain (okta -> proxy -> ingress -> app).

Short-term mitigation attempted: rollback header-rewrite on identity-proxy; revert ingress cookie policy to previous explicit SameSite=None for internal hosts; restart runbook service pods to flush cached header parsing state. Results: successful restores of login for affected users in us-east.

Risk assessment: Rollback safe; long-term fix will require code changes to session validation and additional test coverage across header reordering scenarios.
resolution:
Workaround applied: Rolled back the identity-proxy header-rewrite change (2026-03-12 03:15 UTC) and reverted ingress cookie policy to enforce SameSite=None for internal domains. Restarted runbook-service and console pods to clear any header parser state.

Permanent fix planned: (1) Update runbook/console session library to canonicalize headers before signature verification and accept missing/empty x-session-sig with clear error codes. (2) Add e2e test that runs Okta redirect chain with header reordering and HTTP/2 path to prevent regressions. (3) Harden identity-proxy to preserve header ordering or include canonicalization shim.

Rollout plan: Patch session library in canary env -> runbook canary -> 72h monitoring -> global rollout. Identity-proxy patch PR created.

Follow-ups: Create a confluence postmortem and add to the oncall runbook: how to verify and rollback identity-proxy changes. Scheduled a retro with ingress and identity-proxy owners.
